note: How chord symbols become voicings (doc 24, Voice-leading; src/audio/music/voicing.js). byStyle: the shape of an accompaniment, each with voices (the bass plus the upper voices), the bass range and the upper range as MIDI notes (60 is middle C). weights: what the search counts as cost. motion, per semitone an upper voice moves; bassMotion, per semitone the bass moves (lower, the bass may leap); innerLeap, extra per semitone an inner voice moves beyond a whole tone, so inner voices move by step; topLeap, extra per semitone the top voice moves beyond a major third; commonTone, a reward for each note held over; parallel, outer voices moving in parallel fifths or octaves (other pairs count half); lowClose, per semitone two adjacent voices are closer than a fifth when the lower is below lowCloseBelow (48 is C3, doc 24: nothing closer than a fifth below C3); wideGap, per semitone two upper voices are further apart than wideGapSemis; bassTenorMin and bassTenorClose, the open spacing between the bass and the next voice (a fifth at least, doc 24: root and fifth or root and tenth) and its cost per semitone short; missingThird and missingSeventh, for leaving out the chord's third (or suspension) or its seventh or sixth; doubledThird and doubledLeading, for doubling the third or the key's leading tone. semitone, for two neighbouring upper voices a semitone apart, and minorNinth for any two voices a minor ninth apart (a major seventh under the root, the usual culprit); missingColor, for leaving out a named colour tone such as the 9 of maj9 or add9; bassCenter, per semitone the bass sits away from bassHome (41 is F2), so a chord's bass doesn't wander between octaves. The piano ships the middle five octaves (playable A1 to D sharp 7), but doc 24 keeps the music above 60 Hz, so no style's bass goes below B1 (35, about 62 Hz).
